Title: When Seven DeSwapp Hopped
Author: by Bronchelle Parker
Content: Seven DeSwapp was so excited when she woke up `text(early Saturday)` morning. She was going to the beach.

`text(Every summer)`, the DeSwapps took a special family trip to the beach. And `text(every summer)`, Seven’s big brother, Ras, found the best treasures there. `text(Last year)`, he saw dolphins diving into the ocean.
“Eureka,” he would cry when he found a treasure.
Seven called him Ras the Terrific Treasure Finder. This `text(year)`, she wanted to be a Terrific Treasure Finder, too.

“Eureka.” She practiced on her way downstairs with Ras. The night before, she had made a list of all the treasures she wanted to find at the beach. A sandcastle with a moat. A starfish. And a cute baby crab.

But when Seven and Ras got to the living room, Ms. DeSwapp did not look ready for the beach. She was wearing sneakers. Not sandals. And she had on a big backpack. Not a bathing suit. Seven and Ras scratched their heads, trading puzzled looks.
“Surprise,” sang Ms. DeSwapp. She tossed each of them a sleeping bag. “This `text(year)`, we’re kicking it up a notch. Bye-bye, beach. We’re going camping in the mountains.”
“Sweet.” Ras jumped up and down, his dreadlocks dancing about his head.
Seven’s heart sank.
“Are there sandcastles in the mountains, Mama?” she asked.
“No, silly,” giggled Ras. . . .

It was a long drive to the mountains. Seven looked out the window. At `text(first)`, the land looked as flat as the pancakes she ate for breakfast. Then the ground slowly started to rise into giant hills with pointy tops.
Seven closed her eyes and tried to imagine what kind of treasures she would find in the mountains. But all she could think of were sandcastles, starfish, and cute baby crabs. . . .
Ms. DeSwapp stopped at a perfect spot in the woods to camp. Then up, up went their tent. And up, up went their feet as they set out for a big hike.
Seven hiked very carefully, so she wouldn’t miss any treasures.
“Eureka.” She practiced while she searched for treasures over big rocks . . . and under little rocks, too. She searched between the bushy bushes . . . and around the tall, tall trees.
When they reached a tiny stream, Seven took a break from treasure hunting.
“Whew!” she huffed, squatting to sit on a rock.
But just as she did, the rock began to croak like a frog! “Ribbit,” croaked the rock. “Ribbit-ribbit.”
Suddenly, `text(six)` green frogs hopped out from behind the rock.
“Ribbit,” they croaked, happily hopping high.
Soon, Seven joined in the frogs’ fun. “Ribbit,” she croaked, hopping up and down. “Ribbit-ribbit.”
Before long, the DeSwapps were playing a silly game of leapfrog. Seven hopped over Ras. Then she hopped over Ms. DeSwapp. She even hopped over the tiny stream.

Bright yellow butterflies greeted Seven on the other side of the stream. Their soft wings tickled her cheeks as they swirled around her head. Then off they flew towards a loud SHHHH coming from the distance.
It sounded like rain. SHHHH.
Slowly, Seven followed the sound. She crept down the trail on her tiptoes.
Closer and closer she came, until she was standing across from a beautiful waterfall. It looked like buckets of water falling from a big cliff with a SHHHH and landing, drop after drop, in a pool.
It was the most terrific treasure Seven had ever seen.
Just behind her, Ras and Ms. DeSwapp watched the waterfall in wide-eyed amazement.
“Sweet find, Seven,” squealed Ras.
Bursting with excitement, Seven threw her arms in the air. And in a voice loud enough to shake the mountains, she cried, “Eureka!”

:box:`bbtext(Glossary)`

`ultext(eureka)`: a cry of joy when someone finds or discovers something
